messages:
pagerbot: ALERT: high-severity — GPU pool 'eu-west-2-prod' at 98% queue depth, autoscaler failing to add nodes. traces: http://internal.monitor/alert/2412345678 :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Page routed to @maria and @kai (primary oncall). Escalation window: 15m.
maria: I'm on it, joining telemetry now. seeing sustained queue growth + 502s from runtime.
kai: I can grab infra side. initial read — autoscaler logs show repeated 'scale veto: policy cap' and 'scale request queued' around 2412345400.
raj: support reports multiple customers with degraded responses; top customer A saw 5xx rate jump to 12% and p95 latency > 12s. tickets: #INC-1342, #CUST-879.
maria: digging into recent deploys — there was a canary for batching/continuous-batcher rolled yesterday. suspect config drift.
eng_runtime: Confirmed: latest canary changed continuous_batch.window_ms from 40 -> 400 and prefix_cache.ttl from 6h -> 30s in feature/fast-path rollout.
ops_tom: oof that TTL change would exponentially increase prefix cache misses and KV eviction churn. that plus larger batch window could cause evictions and higher GPU memory, reducing active inflight.
sre_lead: Priority: reduce tail latency and stop queue growth. Recommended immediate mitigations: 1) revert batch window change 2) increase scale cap temporarily 3) disable continuous batching for affected model variant.
maria: rolling a rollback for batching config now. command: ```rwctl deploy-config set continuous_batch.window_ms=40 --env prod --service runtime-canary --from-commit HEAD~1```
kai: while rollback rolls, I'm bumping autoscaler cap from 40 -> 70 for eu-west-2-prod: ```autoscalectl set-cap --pool eu-west-2-prod --max 70```
eng_runtime: also pushing TTL back to 6h: ```kvctl set global prefix_cache.ttl=21600 --env prod``` — will take ~30s to propagate.
raj: not sure if we need to drain any hot shards — showing some GPU pods with OOMs and high eviction counts. logs: ```2026-03-14T21:03:11Z runtime kernel: kv_cache evict key=prefix:abcd count=12 mem_delta=-1.2Gi```
ops_tom: plan B if autoscaler still refuses: manual node add and graceful service rollout to balance hot shards.
support_amy: Notifying affected customers with status update. message drafted to CSMs and posted to status.redwood.ai as incident in progress.
maria: rollback applied — continuous_batch.window_ms -> 40. monitoring: queue depth starting to plateau at ~65% now.
kai: autoscaler cap change accepted, new nodes provisioning. seeing 6 new GPU instances requested.
eng_runtime: prefix TTL reverted; cache hit rate climbing from 12% -> 78% over last 90s.
sre_lead: Good. keep monitoring for 30m, look for p95 < 2s and 5xx < 1%. if stable, we can begin scaledown and postmortem.
maria: handing off to @kai for next 45m watch. I'm out for the next meeting. documented steps in the incident doc: http://internals/incident/2412345678.
kai: taking over. I'll coordinate scale down if p95 stays under 2s and queue < 15%. tagging @ops_tom for manual support if needed. :thumbsup:
pagerbot: RESOLVE: queue depth returned to normal after mitigations; final note: root cause appears to be config regression in batching + prefix cache TTL change causing cache missstorm -> GPU memory pressure -> reduced throughput -> autoscaler hit policy caps. postmortem assigned to eng_runtime and sre_lead.
